comments.author: @eyestoenvy
comments.text: The airline industry as it stands here in the U.S., is broken.  How many airlines have failed since deregulation, hundreds?  Big and small, poof, GONE!  And with them go jobs, paychecks, pensions, dreams, etc.  I worked for AA for 10 years and experienced nothing but a nonstop wave of hardships such as lay offs, recalls, contract concessions, union seniority bumping from station (airport) to station, being bumped from shifts, being forced to remain on shift/site in bad weather, etc.  Was the free travel worth it?  F-ck no.  No way.  I mean think about it, how good is such a perk as free travel if you're still too broke to go regardless?  Nope, I wouldn't recommend it to anyone.  Even (once) glamorous jobs like pilots and in-flight crews fall just as hard to the ground amongst the peasants at the gate, ticket counters, baggage rooms, and ramp side.  Once the entire operation goes to hell, etc.  Bankruptcy, like death it is the great equalizer of the airline industry.  Air travel is important, absolutely.  Just like any utility service that we use in our homes or businesses for everyday life.  Hence they should be treated a such.  In other words, regulated once again.  Regulated for their sole purpose as opposed to being profit driven.  Bob Crandall of American Airlines made this claim years ago, and he's been proven RIGHT time after time again.  I'm sorry to see SPIRIT go, I really am.  They gave you what you paid for and the terms were laid out for you prior to purchase.  They gave wings to the poor of this country and enabled them to move about and experience new things.  The brand became iconic both in the skies and down below on the ground.  And on social media?  Forget about it, SPIRIT ruled.  People criticized them but flew them nonetheless, and were (almost always) grateful to have them around.  Farewell, oh flying school bus.  You will be missed.
